_readme: NOTES. Finishing the first container in a room leaves a 📝 on the floor.
Pick it up and someone has written to you.
This is deliberately the cheapest possible NPC: no portrait, no dialogue
tree, no voice acting. A handwritten card delivers most of the presence a
character would, establishes a voice, and doesn't interrupt the quiet loop
the game is actually good at. If the writing lands, THEN consider giving
Keyed by room id. `need` is a list of emoji that must all be filed in
their home container to complete it. If a room has no entry here — or the
listed emoji aren't in this run — a fallback note is generated from
whatever the room actually contains, so every room gets one for free.
`text` is the note. `reply` is what arrives when you finish it.
Keep them to one or two sentences and in the same hand throughout.
_roomShareNote: roomShare — what fraction of a house's rooms start with a SEALED container.
It was effectively 1.0 (every room), which made a locked cupboard the
resting state of the house instead of an event. 0 turns seals off entirely;
a level or size entry can override it with a `quests` number (a fraction,
or a room count if above 1) or `quests: false`.
Rooms without a seal still leave a note — see `fallback` below.
_sealedNote: Used when the note is about the room's SEALED container — the one that
stays shut until you finish something else in the room. This is the
normal case; `fallback` only fires in rooms with no sealed container.

sealed.text: You got the rest of it done, so here's the key bit: the {container} still needs filling.
sealed.reply: The {container} too. That's the whole room, then. Thank you.

fallback.text: Whoever's tidying: if you get the {container} sorted I'll owe you one.
fallback.reply: The {container}. You actually did it. Thank you.

kitchen.text: Milk, eggs, butter — in the fridge before dinner, please. I keep finding them on the counter.
kitchen.reply: Fridge stocked. Dinner is saved. You're a marvel.

garage.text: The wrench, the hammer, the screwdriver. Back on the bench where they live. I've been looking for that hammer since March.
garage.reply: There it is. Since March. Thank you.

bathroom.text: Pills and plasters in the cabinet, before someone needs them in a hurry.
bathroom.reply: Cabinet sorted. Nobody's bleeding. Good day.

office.text: The document, the receipt, the folder. Filing cabinet. I have an appointment on Thursday and I need to find all three.

bedroom.text: Socks, shirt, jeans — in the dresser. I'd like to get dressed tomorrow without an expedition.
bedroom.reply: Dresser done. Tomorrow will be easy.

closet.text: Suitcase and boots on the travel shelf. I'm not saying we're going anywhere. I'm saying we could.
closet.reply: Packed and ready. We could, you know.

attic.text: The picture and the clock, into the memory chest. Careful with the picture.
attic.reply: Both safe. That picture is older than this house.

shed.text: Seedling and the potted one, on the potting bench where they get light.
shed.reply: They'll take now. Give them a month.

secret.text: You found this room, then. The gem and the crown go in the chest. Don't ask.
secret.reply: Locked away again. We never had this conversation.

playroom.text: The puzzle and the kite, in the toy chest. There are eleven hundred pieces and I have found four of them with my feet.
playroom.reply: Toy chest shut. My feet thank you personally.

music.text: Microphone and headphones back on the sound shelf. Nobody in this house has been quiet since we bought that microphone.
music.reply: Sound shelf sorted. Blessed, blessed silence.

mudroom.text: Skateboard and skates on the gear rack, not in the doorway. I have views about this that you have heard before.
mudroom.reply: Gear rack loaded. Nobody breaks an ankle tonight.

cellar.text: The wine glass and the good bottle, on the rack. The bottle is for an occasion. This is not the occasion.
cellar.reply: Back on the rack. One day, the occasion. Not today.

observatory.text: Telescope and compass into the optics case before the damp gets at the lenses. Clear sky on Thursday.
observatory.reply: Both cased. Thursday, then — bring a coat, it's cold up here.
